primary_topics: Opening remarks by CJP at the first formal meeting of the FLP Scholars Society (FLPSS), July 11, 2020 -- via Zoom, during the COVID-19 pandemic
Practical guidance for the Society's founding: Vision and Mission Statements, Fundamental Principles, Core Values, and Program of Action
The FLPSS as an enduring bond: transcending geography, career, religion, gender and politics -- united only by the liberty-and-prosperity philosophy
Advance notice of new FLP programs: the ESME graduate fellowship expansion and the Entrepreneurship Fund of ~P1 billion for MSMEs
sub_topics: Context: first formal FLPSS meeting via Zoom; COVID as the immediate cause but also 'a blessing' as it ushers the 'new normal' and 'the precursor of the normal things in the DiGi Age'

FLPSS membership exclusivity: only those who passed FLP's strict screening and personal interviews by SC justices; only those who personify, believe in and commit to liberty-and-prosperity philosophy; selected from best law schools in the country

Prophetic commissioning: 'In the next 10 to 20 years, you would be the leaders of our country... the chief justices, justices, judges, super law practitioners, Cabinet members, solons and even Presidents'
Vision statement guidance: short, comprehensive statement of what the Society stands for

Mission statement guidance -- three concrete examples: (1) Strengthen bond of friendship and unity (Wikipedia-style directory); (2) Give back to FLP -- encourage schoolmates to apply, donate to create more scholarships; minimum membership fees proposed (free for undergraduates, P2,000/year for graduates); (3) Help FLP create, administer and fund other programs for liberty and prosperity
Fundamental Principles and Core Values: democracy, freedom, integrity, ethics, free enterprise, hard work, patriotism, excellence, innovation, creativity, and other DiGi Age virtues

Enduring bond across diversity: different towns, social strata, financial situations, political parties -- united by the philosophy; Society must be neutral in political, commercial, social, religious, economic matters

Focus discipline: many competing causes exist (scholarships for the poor, poverty alleviation, climate change, health, disaster assistance) -- laudable but the FSS must NOT divert its attention to these side endeavors; others will take them up

CJP's role and Susan/Joel's roles: CJP is 'ancient lolo, alalay or assistant' or Adviser; Susan Gavino as FLP Coordinator; Joel Emerson Gregorio as FLP Corporate Secretary and Coordinator; FLPSS President invited to attend July 16 online FLP Annual Meeting as observer

Leadership succession: CJP hopes future FLPSS members will be elected FLP Board Members and Officers -- the older generation will 'pass away someday and will be glad to turn over gradually to you the leadership'

New FLP programs previewed: ESME (entrepreneurship, sustainability, management, economics) graduate fellowships -- proposed to AIM; Entrepreneurship Fund of about P1 billion for MSMEs with social impact but no bank access

stances.claim: The FLPSS must remain disciplined in its focus -- exclusively on the liberty-and-prosperity philosophy -- and must not divert to side causes like climate change, poverty alleviation, or disaster assistance, however laudable. 'There would be enough people, enough organizations, and enough groups that would take them up.' Focused institutional identity is the Society's primary organizational obligation.
stances.rhetorical_move: focus-discipline argument: institutional identity requires explicit exclusion of competing causes, even laudable ones

stances.claim: The Society must be politically neutral within its institutional space, though members may participate in partisan politics personally. 'Inside the Society, we should be always united in our common pursuit of liberty, prosperity and the rule of law. We should have no political, ideological, social, religious, gender or even medical issues that will deflect us from our common vision and mission.'
stances.rhetorical_move: internal-unity-with-external-freedom design: the Society as a protected non-partisan space

stances.claim: The COVID-19 pandemic -- though it forced the FLPSS inaugural to Zoom -- is actually a blessing, not merely an obstacle: it inaugurates the 'new normal' and 'the precursor of the normal things in the DiGi Age.' The disruption accelerates the Society into the modality that will define its future operations.
stances.rhetorical_move: disruption-as-acceleration: reframing a COVID constraint as a structural advantage

notable_anecdotes: CJP as 'ancient lolo, alalay or assistant': he explicitly says he 'cannot be a member because, unlike you, I do not possess the qualifications and did not pass the stringent screening requirements for membership. I suppose I am just your ancient lolo, alalay or assistant, a title I would gladly have. But if you want to be high falutin, you can promote me as your Adviser.'

The Wikipedia-style directory idea: for the first Mission item (strengthening unity), CJP suggests 'an easy-to-update directory (like Wikipedia) showing the members' personal circumstances, residences, telephones, email addresses and his or her employment or career, etc.' -- a practical, concrete first deliverable.
The P2,000/year membership fee proposal: 'free for undergraduates and P2,000 a year for graduates, without prejudice but with thanks for donations from the more generous and more well-to-do members.'

The leadership succession vision: 'I trust that one of you, and later on, several of you will be elected Board Members and/or Officers of the FLP because we, of the older generation, will pass away someday and will be glad to turn over gradually to you the leadership of the Foundation.'

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered July 11, 2020 via Zoom at the first formal meeting of the FLP Scholars Society (FLPSS), this opening address by CJP -- who immediately frames the COVID-forced online format as 'a blessing' that inaugurates 'the normal things in the DiGi Age' -- offers practical founding guidance. He emphasizes FLPSS membership exclusivity (only those who passed FLP's stringent screening by SC justices and committed to the liberty-and-prosperity philosophy from the best law schools in the country), reiterates the prophetic commissioning ('in the next 10 to 20 years, you would be the leaders of our country -- chief justices, justices, legislators, cabinet members, even Presidents'), and provides specific guidance: craft Vision and Mission Statements first; the Mission should include (1) strengthening unity via a Wikipedia-style directory and minimum fees (free for undergraduates, P2,000/year for graduates), (2) giving back by recruiting future applicants and donating for more scholarships, and (3) helping FLP create new programs. He specifies the Fundamental Principles and Core Values: democracy, freedom, integrity, ethics, free enterprise, hard work, patriotism, excellence, innovation, creativity, and DiGi Age virtues. He insists on focus discipline -- the Society must NOT divert to side causes like climate change, poverty alleviation or disaster assistance, however laudable ('there would be enough people... that would take them up') -- and on internal political neutrality ('minds are like parachutes -- they work only when they are open'). He defines his own role self-deprecatingly as 'ancient lolo, alalay or assistant' (or Adviser, 'if you want to be high falutin'), invites the President to attend the July 16 FLP Board Meeting as observer, and previews two new FLP programs: ESME graduate fellowships and the Entrepreneurship Fund of about P1 billion for MSMEs. He closes with the succession vision: future FLPSS members will be elected to the FLP Board, 'because we, of the older generation, will pass away someday and will be glad to turn over gradually to you the leadership.'
